headline:
Tools shaped around

lead: We consolidate work scattered across spreadsheets and services into one internal system — designing screens, permissions, and data structures for the ops and admin flows your team actually runs.

meta.v: Teams with recurring ops and admin work

overviewTitle:
Build an internal system
for how the team works.
overviewBody: Many teams still run operations across spreadsheets, chat, email, and multiple SaaS tools.
When intake, status, approvals, inventory, schedules, and customer records live in different places, people become the integration layer.
INTERNAL TOOLS turns that into screens and data structures that match your real process — not a customer-facing product, but a tool your team uses every day.
problemsTitle: When an internal tool becomes necessary.

problems.d: Requests and records live across sheets, chat, mail, and tools.
People manually pass work whenever ownership or stage changes.
It’s hard to see what’s in progress at a glance.
Reviews and approvals stall across chat and email.
Sensitive data sits in shared sheets everyone can open.
There’s little record of who changed what, and when.
Spreadsheet ops break down as people and volume grow.
Off-the-shelf SaaS doesn’t match the team process.

capsTitle: We compose the functions your work needs.

caps.d: Receive requests through defined forms and flows.
Manage status, owners, and priority in one place.
Lock review and approval into clear stages.
Bring operational status into one view.
Structure internal reference data and records.
Split screens and permissions by role.
Connect services and data you already use.

useCases.d: A console for requests, progress, and ownership.
Standard intake forms with shared status for teams.
Systemize budget, content, or access approvals.
Manage client work, schedules, and deliverables internally.
A pipeline tool simplified to your sales/inquiry process.
One board for production, review, and publish status.
An ops board combining metrics from multiple sources.

flow.d:
Requests and data enter via forms, APIs, or files.
Required fields and attachments are validated first.

Type, priority, and owner rules assign the work.
The next stage and approval path are set automatically.

Teams process, edit, and approve in-screen.
Comments, files, and status changes stay in one flow.

Status changes notify the people who need to know.
Delivered through Slack, email, or in-app alerts.

Who changed what, and when, is stored as history.
Outcomes are kept for audit and replay.

Dashboards, lists, and filters show current state.
Bottlenecks, delays, and throughput in one view.

scopeTitle: A guide to understanding project complexity.
scopeLead: Not fixed packages — a reference for scoping and quoting what you need.
timeLead: Features, integrations, permission structure, and existing data can change duration.
priceTitle: We quote only the scope you need.
priceNote: Final quote is set after we review your current process and required features.
extTitle: Costs that may sit outside Newon’s build fee
secTitle: Internal tools start with access and data.
secLead: When sensitive information is involved, we design for role-based access, least privilege, and only the logs you need. Security requirements are confirmed before kickoff.

faqs.q: Isn’t Notion or a spreadsheet enough?
faqs.a: It can be early on. When permissions, status, approvals, history, and integrations get complex, a dedicated internal tool is often more stable.

faqs.q: How is this different from customizing SaaS?
faqs.a: SaaS is great for speed, but may not match your process. INTERNAL TOOLS starts from your real flow and builds the screens and rules you need.

faqs.q: Do we need a large system from day one?
faqs.a: No. We recommend starting with the most repetitive, high-cost work flow in a focused scope.

faqs.q: Can you migrate existing sheet data?
faqs.a: Yes. Migration scope depends on data cleanliness and structure, and may be scoped separately.
We can build a mobile-friendly UI. Native-app needs are confirmed as separate scope.

faqs.q: Can AI or automation be included?
faqs.a: Yes. We often extend from clear areas first — classification, summaries, alerts, and sync.
We align on access, data range, and logs. Hosting and auth follow your environment and policy.

faqs.q: Can you maintain and extend after launch?
faqs.a: Yes. Feature additions, integration changes, and ops support can be scoped separately.
